_comment: Two cameras in one process. Each has its own virtual fence, because a low laptop camera and a high phone camera see completely different geometry. Plain YOLO is stateless, so the model loads once and both feeds share it. A camera that is not answering is skipped at startup rather than stalling the fleet.
_location_note: 'location' is optional and only feeds the map - a camera without one runs identically. lat/lon are WGS84 degrees. 'bearing' is the compass direction the camera faces and 'fov' its horizontal field of view; together they draw a wedge on the map showing which way it points. That wedge is a claim about aim, NOT measured coverage - a ridge or a parked truck takes most of it away. Leave bearing out rather than guessing it. The coordinates below are placeholders for a development machine, not a real post.

cameras._note: IP Webcam app on the phone - update the IP if it changes

_geofence_note: Areas drawn on the map, in lat/lon. These are NOT the virtual fences in config/zones-*.json - those live in frame coordinates and cannot be placed on a map without a surveyed homography per camera. Nothing in the running pipeline tests detections against these yet; they group cameras by sector and give the map areas to draw.
